original.description: Development of a compact optical atomic clock module (physics package) for PNT applications. The activity will design, manufacture,and test an Engineering Model (EM) of a chip-scale optical clock exploiting an atomic optical transition to achieve 10 improved stability (target timing drift 10-30 ns/day) versus existing microwave clocks. The clock will provide a stabilized optical frequencyoutput in a low-power (< 5 W), compact device. Tasks include detailed thermo-mechanical design for robust operation in harsh environments, definition of low-power control electronics requirements and autonomous operation algorithms, assembly of the optical clock physics package, and development of Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) to control and test the EM. The EM will undergo performance verification in ambient and thermal conditions to demonstrate its stability, targeting TRL 4-5 and paving the way for future space-qualified ultra-stable timing solutions for navigation and timing systems.

original.description: ANUBIS (Asteroid NUdging By Ion-beam Shepherding) is a potential future Planetary Defence Cornerstone aiming to demonstrate the "ion beam shepherd" concept, which makes use of ion thrusters to deflect asteroids. The concept is of great interest to Planetary Defence and the scientific community, as demonstrated by various assessments, and in particular highlighted by the UN Space Mission Planning Advisory Group (SMPAG). The concept is one of the most promising candidates for deflecting potentially hazardous asteroids, when there is time enough to apply this technology.

original.description: Objective:To develop a portable modem that can be easily integrated in an existing optical ground station to make it compatible with ESTOL specificationsTargeted Improvements:Increased interoperability between existing optical ground stations and future satellite systems (e.g., HydRON).Description:There are a number of existing or planned optical ground stations (OGSs) that are currently used for scientific missions or to demonstrate quantum technologies. Those OGSs are not compliant to the ESA Specifications for Terabit/s Optical Links (ESTOL). To maximise the benefit of early Member State investments, the activity shall develop an upgrade kit" for multiple existing OGS infrastructures. An easy-to-integrate modem will facilitate the upgrade of such existing or planned OGSsand increase their interoperability with future commercial and institutional systems that will adopt ESTOL and its evolutions.Thisactivity shall develop a portable breadboard for an ESTOL-compliant modem. In the scope of the activity, it shall be assumed that thetarget existing OGSs have already been developed in terms of optical elements (e.g., aperture, adaptive optics, etc.) in order tobecompatible with ESTOL. The portable modem shall be connected to the optical part of the OGS by optical fibre, and it shall implement both transmit and receive functionalities. The modem breadboard shall come with a GUI and an interface control document to facilitate its fast and easy integration and use. The functionalities of the portable modem shall be validated in the Contractor's laboratory and in an existing selected OGS.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). original.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a mechanism for an optical ground station that can adjust the beam's divergence during the link sessionwithout link interruption and whilst maintaining the optical pointing accuracy.TargetedImprovements:To enable dynamic adjustment of the beam divergence without needing optical realignment. This will enable real-time optimisation of the link based onthe elevation angle and the turbulence conditions. Eventually, integrating the beacon capabilities with the communications beam.Description: Alignment of the optical system at an optical ground station is usually needed before a link session, especially if the optical configuration (beam divergence)has changed. Links to Low-Earth Orbit are highly dynamic, ranging for very small elevation angles up to zenith, and atmospheric turbulence conditionsevolving during a link session. It is essential that for links targeting optical feeder applications the ground-space connectivity must be maintained.Furthermore, ground-to-space links usually make use of a beacon during the acquisition phase. For these reasons, developing a mechanism that allowsfor real-time beam-divergence adjustment without the need to re-align the optical components is considered very useful.Some of the off-the-shelf components used in optical ground stations are limited in accuracy and optical power, and therefore not suitable for an on-skyreal-time adjustment of the beam divergence. This activity shall evaluate the state-of-the-art of mechanisms, with their limitations on accuracy, precisionand maximum supported power. The design and development of an engineering model shall demonstrate the capabilities of the mechanism. This goalcan be achieved either in the laboratory with realistic interfaces or at an optical ground station.

original.description: To develop an active antenna combined software and hardware demonstrator representative of a LEO satellite payload by exploiting advanced strategies for real time dynamically managing radio resources.Description: On-board satellite resource allocationstrategiesare essential for managing the distribution of limited resources from the antennas to multiple user terminals. These strategies involve dynamic allocation techniques that can adjust in real-time based on traffic demand. However, in dense traffic scenarios like onboard LEO satellites, these strategies face significant challenges. The high volume of demand can lead to congestion, resulting in increased latency and reduced QoS. Additionally, the limited on-board processing capability challenges the satellite's ability to efficiently manage traffic which leads to degraded antenna performance. Considering these challenges, the objective of this activity isto develop an active antenna combined software and hardware demonstrator representative of a LEO satellite payload by exploiting advanced strategies for dynamically managing radio resources, i.e. beamforming for real time tracking and coverage change combined with power and bandwidth allocation. Resource allocation should be defined as an optimization problem, considering factors like channelconditions, user demands, interference levels, and power constraints. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Derive real-time complex coefficients, using optimization strategies for the beamforming network. - Emulate users' movement and channel changes for proactive beam steering. - Develop models to detect and classify interference sources and use optimization techniquesfor mitigation. - Manufacture and test a proof-of-concept hardware demonstrator with a limited size active phased array and associated adaptivebeamforming, mounted on a mechanically movable platform with additional antennas located in fixed positions.

Considering these challenges, the objective of this activity isto develop an active antenna combined software and hardware demonstrator representative of a LEO satellite payload by exploiting advanced strategies for dynamically managing radio resources, i.e. beamforming for real time tracking and coverage change combined with power and bandwidth allocation. Resource allocation should be defined as an optimization problem, considering factors like channelconditions, user demands, interference levels, and power constraints. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Derive real-time complex coefficients, using optimization strategies for the beamforming network. - Emulate users' movement and channel changes for proactive beam steering. - Develop models to detect and classify interference sources and use optimization techniquesfor mitigation. - Manufacture and test a proof-of-concept hardware demonstrator with a limited size active phased array and associated adaptivebeamforming, mounted on a mechanically movable platform with additional antennas located in fixed positions.
